title: Specified evaluation and exact tensor inverse pair for a sheaf line
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ the abelian category of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with its symmetric monoidal constraints [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $P$ be locally free of rank one: every object has a covering on whose slices $P\cong R$. Put $P^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(P,R)$, $T(M)=M\otimes_RP$, and $S(M)=M\otimes_RP^\vee$.

The sheaf $P^\vee$ is locally free of rank one, and the specified evaluation $e:P\otimes_RP^\vee\to R$, $x\otimes\phi\mapsto\phi(x)$, is an isomorphism. On every trivializing slice with basis $p$ and dual $p^\vee$ it and its inverse satisfy
$$e((ap)\otimes(bp^\vee))=ab,\qquad e^{-1}(a)=(ap)\otimes p^\vee.$$
These formulas agree under every change of basis $p'=up$, $(p')^\vee=u^{-1}p^\vee$ with $u$ a unit.

Reassociation followed by $e$, and by evaluation after symmetry, defines natural isomorphisms $a:ST\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ and $b:TS\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. Their local formulas are
$$a_M((x\otimes cp)\otimes dp^\vee)=cdx,\quad a_M^{-1}(x)=(x\otimes p)\otimes p^\vee,$$
$$b_M((x\otimes dp^\vee)\otimes cp)=cdx,\quad b_M^{-1}(x)=(x\otimes p^\vee)\otimes p.$$
For every $M$ the identities $b_{TM}\circ T(a_M^{-1})=1_{TM}$ and $S(b_M)\circ a_{SM}^{-1}=1_{SM}$ hold. Thus $T,S$ are inverse additive exact equivalences: they preserve finite limits and finite colimits; in particular $P,P^\vee$ are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. If $R$ is a sheaf of algebras over a commutative ring $B$, then $T,S$ are $B$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor] for the sectionwise scalar action on module morphisms, and the displayed evaluation, inverse, $a,b$ and their inverses have $B$-linear components.

proof.text: On each trivializing slice choose p as the inverse image of 1 and phi as the trivialization map. Naturality of the inverse trivialization shows that every restricted section is a scalar multiple of the restriction of p. A morphism to the unit is determined by its value on these generators. Hence evaluation at p identifies the dual sections with the coefficient ring, compatibly with restriction, giving the dual trivialization.

source.place: Tags 0B8Q (lemma-invertible-is-locally-free-rank-1), first proof paragraph, and 0B8N (lemma-invertible), evaluation and exact tensor equivalence; explicit inverse and triangle normalizations extracted from old proof steps 1--3.

proof.text: Construct the evaluation bilinear map sectionwise and check naturality. The sheafification adjunction and tensorObjIsoSheafification induce the sheaf evaluation map. The sectionwise map is bijective wherever a trivialization exists, by TensorProduct.lift_bijective_of_forall_eq_smul and the preceding generator argument. Thus it is locally injective and locally surjective. Module sheafification inverts such maps, so the sheaf evaluation is an isomorphism. Its value on every pure tensor follows from the adjunction unit identity.

proof.text: Use the canonical reassociation, tensor evaluation and right unitor composites defining cancellation. The existing pure-tensor map, associator and braiding formulas, together with the adjunction-induced lax monoidal right-unitor formula, compute cancellation on pure triples. Apply the inverse identity and injectivity of each isomorphism component to obtain the specified inverse formulas. Scalar bilinearity cancels a unit and its inverse, proving all basis-change formulas.

proof.text: Maps out of a sheaf tensor are determined on sheafified presheaf pure tensors: precompose with tensorObjIsoSheafification inverse, apply the sheafification adjunction and presheaf tensor extensionality. Check the first triangle on pure tensors after restricting along a trivializing covering sieve. Write the P factor as cp and use the cancellation and inverse formulas. The composite becomes c times the original pure tensor. Separatedness of the underlying module sheaf proves equality globally. Build an equivalence with exactly these unit and counit isomorphisms; Mathlib Equivalence.unit_inverse_comp gives the second triangle from the first.

proof.text: The two cancellation natural isomorphisms exhibit tensoring by P and its dual as inverse equivalences. Equivalences preserve finite limits and colimits, and tensor is additive by the existing monoidal preadditivity instance. Transport exactness to the explicit site tensor through siteSheafTensorRightIso, proving flatness for both factors.

proof.text: On a pure tensor, tensoring the scalar multiple of a morphism multiplies its first factor by the scalar section. Bilinearity identifies this with the scalar multiple of the tensor map. Pure-tensor extensionality proves linearity over the global-section ring. All displayed components are bundled module-sheaf morphisms.
